newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Moslem rebels kill eight Algerian villagers - report.
newsitem.headline: Moslem rebels kill eight Algerian villagers - report.

text.p: Moslem guerrillas cut the throats of six men and decapitated two women south of Algiers in the latest massacre of Algerian villagers, an Algerian newspaper said on Thursday.
The rebel gunmen raided Djebara village in Medea province, 70 km (45 miles) south of Algiers, on Monday night cutting the throats of the men and abducting two women, said El Watan newspaper.
The women were found later, decapitated near the village, said El Watan.
The news of the killings came four days before the end of campaigning for Algeria's parliamentary elections to be held on June 5.
Moslem rebels slaughtered 30 villagers in Chebli hamlet, some 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers hours before the beginning of poll campaigning on May 15.
The worst massacre in Algeria's five years of violence was in April when rebels killed at least 93 villagers, including 43 women and girls, according to the authorities.

About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's strife pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces since the authorities cancelled a 1992 general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
